tags.problem: couples destroying each other through patterns neither can see
tags.evidence: Built the Love Lab to make invisible relationship patterns visible through physiological monitoring, identified the Four Horsemen that predict divorce with 90%+ accuracy

tags.problem: children growing up watching their parents' marriage die in slow motion
tags.evidence: Research showed that couples' conflict patterns directly shape children's emotional regulation, leading Gottman to develop emotion coaching for parents

tags.problem: adults crying out for love in a language their partner cannot hear
tags.evidence: Built EFT around the insight that couple arguments are attachment cries disguised as complaints, and that the real questions are 'Are you there for me? Can I count on you?'

tags.problem: therapists treating relationship pain like a communication problem when it is a survival response
tags.evidence: Showed that couple distress activates the same brain regions as physical pain, and that treating it as a skills deficit misses the neurobiology entirely

tags.problem: repeating your parents' worst patterns with the person you chose to love
tags.evidence: Developed Imago theory from his own divorce, showing that we unconsciously choose partners who resemble the caregivers who wounded us

tags.problem: childhood wounds running your adult relationships without your permission
tags.evidence: Mapped how unmet childhood needs create an 'Imago' template that drives partner selection and conflict patterns in adult relationships

tags.problem: men drowning in depression they have been trained not to name
tags.evidence: Identified 'covert depression' in men, showing it manifests as rage, addiction, and workaholism rather than sadness, making it invisible to standard diagnostic criteria

tags.problem: boys having their emotional range amputated before they are old enough to protest
tags.evidence: Documented how boys are systematically trained out of vulnerability starting around age five, tracing this to his own father's violence and depression

tags.problem: people who genuinely love each other still feeling completely unloved
tags.evidence: Observed in decades of pastoral counselling that couples expressing love in mismatched 'languages' feel unloved despite both partners' genuine effort

tags.problem: important emotional knowledge being locked behind therapy fees nobody can afford
tags.evidence: Created a five-category framework simple enough to spread through word of mouth and free online quizzes, reaching people who would never see a therapist

tags.problem: your nervous system picking a fight before your mouth opens
tags.evidence: Built PACT therapy around the insight that couples' bodies enter threat responses before conscious thought, and that the therapist must read physiology, not just words

tags.problem: attachment science being too clinical for the people who need it most
tags.evidence: Translated academic attachment categories into Anchor/Island/Wave language accessible to ordinary couples and simplified neuroscience into Wired for Love

tags.problem: the most important things in life being the ones nobody teaches you
tags.evidence: Founded The School of Life to teach relationships, work, anxiety, and death, subjects that formal education ignores entirely

tags.problem: Romanticism teaching people that love should be effortless, then leaving them alone when it is not
tags.evidence: Argued in The Course of Love that the Romantic myth of effortless love is the primary cause of relationship failure, because it makes difficulty feel like proof of the wrong partner

tags.problem: addicted people being punished for pain nobody ever treated
tags.evidence: 12 years working with Vancouver's most addicted patients, hearing childhood trauma in every history, reframing 'Why the addiction?' as 'Why the pain?'

tags.problem: a society producing epidemics of anxiety and depression and calling itself normal
tags.evidence: The Myth of Normal argued that Western culture itself is the pathology, treating symptoms while ignoring the conditions that produce them

tags.problem: a world treating addiction as a chemical problem when it is a loneliness problem
tags.evidence: Popularised Rat Park experiment showing rats in social environments ignore morphine, and travelled nine countries documenting the connection between isolation and addiction

tags.problem: governments putting people in cages for being in pain
tags.evidence: Traced the war on drugs from Anslinger's 1930s racism through to present-day mass incarceration, documenting Portugal's successful decriminalisation as the counter-example

tags.problem: the addiction field lying to itself about what addiction actually is
tags.evidence: Challenged both the moral model and the disease model by proposing addiction as a developmental learning disorder, grounded in her own lived experience and neuroscience research

tags.problem: teenagers being tortured in treatment programmes their parents paid for
tags.evidence: Help at Any Cost investigated abusive youth treatment facilities, documenting deaths and physical abuse in programmes operating without regulatory oversight

tags.problem: an entire field of science built on assumptions nobody bothered to test
tags.evidence: Ran controlled experiments showing most crack and meth users chose small cash rewards over another hit, directly contradicting the dominant 'irresistibly addictive' narrative

tags.problem: Black communities being destroyed by a drug war designed to destroy them
tags.evidence: Grew up in poverty in Miami during the crack era, entered neuroscience to prove the drug-war narrative, then watched his own data dismantle everything he had believed

tags.problem: women being sold alcohol as self-care and then shamed when they cannot stop
tags.evidence: Quit Like a Woman documented how the alcohol industry markets specifically to women as empowerment, while the recovery industry then demands surrender and powerlessness

tags.problem: recovery programmes designed for 1930s white men being treated as the only option in 2020
tags.evidence: Found the scientific evidence for AA surprisingly thin, built Tempest as an alternative that replaced surrender-based language with agency-based tools

tags.problem: recovery being treated as something shameful instead of something heroic
tags.evidence: Used his global celebrity platform to rewrite the 12 steps in contemporary language and testified before the UK parliament about his own crack and heroin addiction

tags.problem: famous people going through the darkest moments of their lives with cameras rolling and nobody helping
tags.evidence: Publicly described his own addiction spiralling while maintaining a career in entertainment, then used that visibility to advocate for abstinence-based treatment

tags.problem: alcoholics dying alone because nobody believed one drunk could help another
tags.evidence: Founded AA on the principle that mutual aid between alcoholics was more powerful than any medical or spiritual intervention, grew it to 2 million members in 180 countries

tags.problem: building something that outlives you by removing yourself from it
tags.evidence: Designed anonymity and anti-personality principles into AA's structure, ensuring the movement survived its founders without a CEO, board, or marketing budget

tags.problem: old age being treated as a disease instead of a phase of life
tags.evidence: Elderhood argued that medicine has no developmental framework for the 30-40 years after 65, and that geriatrics is the least-funded specialty despite serving the fastest-growing demographic

tags.problem: a country with 50 million people over 65 and only 7,000 doctors trained to care for them
tags.evidence: Documented the geriatrics recruitment crisis, showing that medical students avoid the field because it pays less and carries less prestige

tags.problem: old people dying of loneliness in buildings designed for efficiency instead of life
tags.evidence: Introduced animals, plants, and children to Chase Memorial Nursing Home and saw mortality drop 15%, then built Green House homes to replace institutional care entirely

tags.problem: nursing homes warehousing people instead of caring for them
tags.evidence: Named loneliness, helplessness, and boredom as the 'three plagues' of institutional care and proved through the Eden Alternative that addressing them reduced mortality and drug costs

tags.problem: the women who care for our parents being paid poverty wages with no protections
tags.evidence: Won the first Domestic Workers' Bill of Rights in New York State in 2010, covering 200,000 nannies, housekeepers, and elder care workers

tags.problem: domestic workers being explicitly excluded from labour protections since the 1930s because of who they were
tags.evidence: Organised workers excluded from the NLRA and FLSA, exclusions originally designed to deny protections to Black and immigrant workers

tags.problem: a country approaching a caregiving crisis and treating it as a personal family problem instead of infrastructure
tags.evidence: The Age of Dignity framed elder care as an infrastructure problem on the scale of the interstate highway system, connecting domestic workers' rights to the aging crisis

tags.problem: a society warehousing its most experienced people at exactly the age they have the most to give
tags.evidence: Built Encore.org and Experience Corps to deploy people over 55 as tutors and mentors, with Johns Hopkins research showing health benefits for the volunteers themselves

tags.problem: old and young people being segregated into separate worlds that impoverish both
tags.evidence: How to Live Forever documented the damage of age-segregated housing and championed intergenerational programmes as the repair

tags.problem: disabled people being locked out of buildings, schools, and jobs by a world designed without them
tags.evidence: Sued for the right to teach after being denied a licence because her wheelchair made her 'a fire hazard,' then led the 25-day Section 504 sit-in

tags.problem: an entire population's civil rights sitting unsigned on a bureaucrat's desk
tags.evidence: Led 150 disabled activists in the longest occupation of a federal building in US history to force the signing of Section 504

tags.problem: disabled people being used as motivational props for people who can walk
tags.evidence: Coined 'inspiration porn' in her TEDxSydney talk, calling out images of disabled people doing ordinary things captioned to make non-disabled people feel better

tags.problem: being given an achievement award for nothing except existing with a disability
tags.evidence: Nominated for a community achievement award at age 15 for no accomplishment other than attending school while disabled

tags.problem: every digital system being built as if blind and deaf people do not exist
tags.evidence: Advocated for website and app accessibility under the ADA, arguing that an inaccessible website is the digital equivalent of stairs at a building entrance

tags.problem: the world calling disability a limitation when the real limitation is the design
tags.evidence: Responded to dinner-party sympathy by asking whether the guest 'suffered' from not being able to echolocate like a bat, reframing disability as the presence of barriers, not the absence of ability

tags.problem: disabled people being told they are too broken to contribute
tags.evidence: The Department of Rehabilitation called him 'too severely disabled to ever work.' He later became Director of that same agency.

tags.problem: disabled people having their lives run by institutions that see patients instead of people
tags.evidence: Founded the first Centre for Independent Living in 1972, based on the principle that disabled people are the experts on their own lives

tags.problem: disabled people's stories being told by everyone except disabled people
tags.evidence: Built the Disability Visibility Project as a StoryCorps partnership to collect first-person disability narratives, then edited an anthology that centred disabled voices exclusively

tags.problem: a pandemic treating ventilator users as expendable
tags.evidence: Dedicated Year of the Tiger to 'all the disabled people who didn't survive the pandemic, not because of COVID but because of ableism'

tags.problem: the poorest people on earth being denied credit not because they are risky but because they are poor
tags.evidence: Lent $27 to 42 women making bamboo stools, got every cent back, and built Grameen Bank to over $30 billion in loans with a 98% repayment rate

tags.problem: women trapped in poverty by moneylenders charging rates that guarantee they stay poor
tags.evidence: Found women in Jobra earning two cents a day because usurious lending ate all their margins, then built a bank owned by borrowers with 97% women members

tags.problem: financial literacy being taught in a language designed to make ordinary people feel stupid
tags.evidence: Built The Budgetnista with an editorial rule: 'If my mother wouldn't understand this sentence, I rewrite it.' Over a million women participated in her free Live Richer Challenge

tags.problem: Black women being invisible to the financial education industry
tags.evidence: Built a financial education platform specifically for women, especially Black women, after losing her own savings in 2008 and finding no resources that spoke to her experience

tags.problem: millions of people being financially responsible but financially invisible because the system does not recognise how they manage money
tags.evidence: Formalised lending circles (tandas) by reporting payments to credit bureaus, making an existing practice visible to a system that had always ignored it

tags.problem: growing up without a Social Security number and being unable to open a bank account in the country you call home
tags.evidence: Crossed the border at age nine undocumented, grew up financially competent but financially invisible, and built Mission Asset Fund from that lived experience

tags.problem: people pretending to afford a life that is bankrupting them because nobody taught them how money works
tags.evidence: Ran 'Can I Afford It?' on CNBC for 13 years, telling people to their faces on national television that they could not afford the purchase they wanted to make

tags.problem: a waitress losing seven years of savings because a broker she trusted did not explain the risk
tags.evidence: Lost $50,000 to a Merrill Lynch broker who invested her savings in high-risk options without proper disclosure, then built her entire career on the outrage

tags.problem: ordinary families drowning in debt they were told was normal
tags.evidence: Went bankrupt at 26 from leveraged real estate, rebuilt using total debt elimination, and taught the debt snowball to millions through Financial Peace University

tags.problem: a culture that normalises borrowing money for everything and calls it financial sophistication
tags.evidence: Built a media empire on the single message that all consumer debt is dangerous, reaching 18 million radio listeners weekly and 10 million Financial Peace University graduates

tags.problem: women taking care of everyone else's money and neglecting their own
tags.evidence: Women and Money argued that women's financial neglect of themselves is a specific emotional pattern, not just a knowledge gap

tags.problem: a credit system that defines 'creditworthy' around products that exclude the people who need credit most
tags.evidence: MacArthur Fellowship citation highlighted his insight that millions of Americans are not financially irresponsible but financially invisible

tags.problem: a doctor buying classical CDs compulsively while his patients waited, and recognising the same wound driving both behaviours
tags.evidence: Disclosed his own compulsive spending in Hungry Ghosts, tracing it to his infancy in Nazi-occupied Budapest when his mother handed him to a stranger to save his life

tags.problem: people with lived experience of addiction being dismissed as unreliable witnesses to their own condition
tags.evidence: Used her own history of cocaine and heroin injection as epistemological authority, arguing she knows when the literature is wrong because the experience does not match

tags.problem: a tenured professor having to disclose heroin use to force people to reconcile their assumptions
tags.evidence: Disclosed regular heroin use in Drug Use for Grown-Ups to confront the gap between the public image of a Columbia professor and assumptions about who uses drugs

tags.problem: a world that sees wheelchairs as tragedies instead of stairs as the problem
tags.evidence: Four decades of advocacy consistently argued that disabled people do not need pity, they need access, from teaching in schools to advising the World Bank

tags.problem: disability being created by inaccessible environments, not by the person's body
tags.evidence: Championed the social model of disability for decades, arguing that the built environment, not the impairment, creates the handicap

tags.problem: aging being treated as a problem to solve instead of a stage of life to design for
tags.evidence: Took his message on a theatrical tour, deliberately choosing non-medical venues to reach audiences who would never attend a geriatrics conference

tags.problem: a culture that believes innovation belongs exclusively to the young
tags.evidence: Created the Purpose Prize to award $100,000 to social innovators over 60, building counter-narratives to the cult of youth in entrepreneurship

tags.problem: sobriety being framed as a confession of failure instead of an act of power
tags.evidence: Reframed quitting drinking as a feminist act in a culture that sells wine as women's empowerment

tags.problem: punishing drug users being treated as policy when it is cruelty
tags.evidence: Told the UK Home Affairs Select Committee that criminalisation was 'cruel and pointless,' testifying from direct personal experience of crack and heroin addiction

tags.problem: a drunk in a hotel lobby with no one to call
tags.evidence: The founding moment of AA was Wilson desperately calling strangers from the Mayflower Hotel in Akron because he needed to talk to another alcoholic to avoid drinking

tags.problem: a preschool teacher earning $39,000 losing everything to a financial con artist because nobody taught her how to spot one
tags.evidence: Lost nearly all her savings in 2008, was also laid off, and rebuilt from zero into a platform that has helped participants save and pay off over $250 million

tags.problem: for-profit imitators turning microfinance into a debt trap
tags.evidence: Acknowledged criticism of microfinance but argued the problems came from for-profit companies that abandoned the social mission and borrower-ownership model

tags.problem: Harvard being designed for people who can see and hear, and nobody noticing until someone who cannot shows up
tags.evidence: Navigated Harvard Law by reverse-engineering access from systems built without her in mind, using a braille display and real-time transcription

tags.problem: the humiliation of bankruptcy teaching you things prosperity never could
tags.evidence: Built a $4 million portfolio on debt by age 26, went bankrupt when the bank called in his notes, and turned the lesson into a 30-year crusade against consumer debt
